correctness.rationale: Let α be the center color. A vertex with color γ in a blade where β occurs a_β times sees a_β+1_{β=α}−1_{β=γ} neighbors of color β. For m=2 either blade vertex fails if its mate has center color, otherwise both pass regardless of whether their own colors agree; the center then imposes the sole global per-color cap n. For m≥3 a monochromatic blade fails (m−1>floor(m/2)). Therefore each β has a witness γ≠β in each blade, giving exactly the stated individual caps h−1 and h. Conversely those caps suffice there and imply the center cap since nh≤floor(nm/2). For a fixed center label the multinomial count gives the restricted sum for m=2 or m![x^m]E_{h−1}E_h^{q−1} per labeled blade for m≥3; only the latter factors by blade. Multiplication by q, then inclusion-exclusion over unused labels, gives A_q and S_q, including the empty-sum and A_0 conventions. At most two colors fail by the total occupancy caps in either case. For m=3 four colors are needed and suffice with each blade a permutation of three other colors; for m=2 two non-center colors can each occur n times; for m≥4 the blade profile (1,h,m−1−h) proves three suffice. At the minimum the maps are surjective, giving the two balanced non-center counts at m=2, permutations at m=3, 6+24 one-blade maps for m=4 and 30 for m=5 with fixed center label. Splitting a nontrivial color class preserves the cap and reaches every larger used-color count. Fresh direct enumeration of neighborhood caps for (n,m)=(2,2),(3,2),(2,3) with q=2,3,4 and (2,4),(2,5) with q=2,3 matched the claimed count, including 18, 60, 144, 2700 and 2700 at the respective minima. These are finite checks, not the universal proof. Replay: RESULT.md lines 45–80; the separate artifacts/verify.py and logged finite replay in VERIFICATION.md were inspected, not run.

value.rationale: This treats a natural vertex-cut family for a recently defined coloring invariant. The exact change from a coupled global constraint for two-vertex blades to independent local constraints for larger blades explains the exceptional optimal palette and supplies labeled palette counts, which the scalar minimum cannot recover.
